acceptance_criteria.given: a scratch Hub, a Haiku agent, and an operator whose ~/.claude/skills holds e2e-loop, handoff and resume
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: py -3.11 scripts/drive/d1015_f454_user_skills.py <project> (written first: all three listed on HEAD)
acceptance_criteria.then: none of the operator's skills is listed
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent is asked to list its skills

acceptance_criteria.given: a directory with a CLAUDE.md rule and a .claude/skills/project-probe skill
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: measured 2026-10-15 by hand (ZEBRA ... project-probe); the argv is pinned by hub/tests/test_runner_commands*.py
acceptance_criteria.then: the reply follows the CLAUDE.md rule and lists project-probe

design:
Tier 2: it changes every Claude agent spawn (cross-cutting). Hazard: an operator who relied on a personal skill or hook inside Hub agents loses it; that is the intent. Rollback: revert.
D1. In `runner_commands._build_claude_command`, the one builder of a Claude agent's argv, beside --strict-mcp-config (F531's precedent for 'only what the Hub gives').
D2. `project,local`, not '': an empty value also drops the project's CLAUDE.md (F195's titler note), which agents need.
D3. One-shot workers (titler, checkpoint) are out of scope: they already pass their own flags and run no tools.

checked: Hand test 2026-10-15: default lists e2e-loop/handoff/resume and plugin skills; project,local lists built-ins only; a project CLAUDE.md rule and project skill still load
Drive on :8031: the Hub agent lists the operator's skills

problem: The Hub spawns `claude` with every setting source, so a Hub agent sees the operator's user-level skills (`~/.claude/skills`), plugin skills and user hooks. In the 2026-09-25 sweep a loop firing ran the operator's `e2e-loop` skill and created loops and commits nobody asked for; the operator's skills include ones that register Windows scheduled tasks. Re-driven 2026-10-15: a Haiku agent lists e2e-loop, handoff, resume, harness-audit and the anthropic-skills plugin among its skills.

requirements.rationale: What a Hub agent may do is the operator's decision through the Hub (charter, posture, tools), not whatever their personal configuration happens to hold.
requirements.statement: Every Claude Code agent run the Hub spawns MUST pass --setting-sources project,local, so the operator's user-level skills, plugins, hooks and settings are not loaded.
The project's CLAUDE.md, its .claude/settings*.json and its .claude/skills MUST still load.

requirements.rationale: A runner flag after the Hub's would win, as in F599.
requirements.statement: A runner's flags MUST NOT carry --setting-sources (refused like the other posture flags).

non_goals: Codex and Copilot user configuration (separate work, Copilot needs the work PC)

summary: Every Claude Code agent run the Hub spawns passes --setting-sources project,local, so it loads the project's CLAUDE.md, settings and skills and none of the operator's personal ~/.claude skills, plugins, hooks or settings (F454).
